Team —

Quick kickoff for our weekly runway handoff focused on StratusAI (deal STRATUS-2026-Q4-02). High-level asks:

- Confirm the committed reserve window they need (weeks + start date).
- Translate that to SKU-level GPU reservations and burst slots.
- Finance: provide an updated burn estimate and margin on proposed commit term.

I've attached the latest forecast (weekly-forecast-10-10.xlsx) and a CSV export of the deal summary. Please reply with:
- Ben: proposed node mix + expected lead time for additional racks if we need to shift pool sizing by >20%.
- Karthik: updated close probability and any changes to payment terms from the buyer.
- Laura: updated monthly burn and any finance gating items for a reserve commitment.

Goal for this thread: lock on a recommended capacity commitment to present to the execs on Tuesday.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Head of Capacity Ops, Redwood Inference

Soojin —

Thanks. Quick read-through and first pass assumptions:

- Proposed node mix for StratusAI (based on their peak QPS in the CSV): 60% A100-80GB (quantized workloads), 40% H100 (low-latency chat).
- Estimated steady-state reservation: 28 x A100 + 18 x H100 (equiv. to 46 unit GPU pool).
- Burst slots: +12 H100-equivalent for demo spikes (hosted bursts on Dedicated).

Lead time: if we need additional racks to move from 46 -> 70 GPUs, procurement lead time is ~6–8 weeks (rack + cabling + onboarding). If we reallocate existing reserved capacity, we can shift within 3–5 business days but would impact other deals' SLAs.

I'll attach a short node-cost snapshot (will upload after this thread). For now, flagging two tradeoffs:
1) If we compress the commit window shorter than 6 months, we should prefer a higher H100 ratio to meet latency SLOs.
2) If legal needs a strict data isolation SLA, on-prem footprint will change the SKU mix.

-Ben
Infrastructure & Fleet, Redwood Inference

Team —

Update from sales call with Stratus (earlier today):

- Close probability moved from 55% -> 72% (legal is finalizing DPA + subtle payment term change).
- They requested a conservative ramp: start with 40 GPUs for first 6 weeks, then scale to 70 over the quarter contingent on performance. They want the option for monthly billing during initial ramp, then a 12-month reserved commit once usage stabilizes.
- They asked explicitly for a 3-week window to validate latency before signing a long-term reserve.

Implication: we should propose a two-stage commit:
A) 6-week pilot reservation (40 GPUs) as a price-locked short commitment with monthly billing.
B) Auto-switch to a 12-month reserved contract for 70 GPUs if pilot metrics meet latency & cost SLOs; include a fallback to 50 GPUs if their usage is below threshold.

I'll push to expand close to 85% by Monday if legal can accept the auto-switch clause.

—Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU Runway Handoff — Weekly Forecast & Commit Window

Thanks all — finance view:

- Attached margin model assumes blended pricing: $7,800/mo per A100-equivalent reserved unit, $12,200/mo per H100-equivalent reserved unit (these are internal list rates).
- For Karthik's two-stage proposal, short pilot (40 GPUs) equates to ~$320k ARR run-rate for the pilot month; full 70 GPU reserve at blended mix is ~ $560k ARR.
- We need legal to sign off on the auto-switch trigger to qualify for amortized capex accounting (finance prefers a deterministic trigger).

Gating questions:
1) Ben — what's the delta in margin if we prioritize H100s for the pilot vs A100-heavy pilot?
2) Marcus — do we have policy precedent for "auto-switch" clauses and any exec approvals required to accept conditional renewals?

If we can get answers to the questions above by Monday EOD, finance can produce a term sheet (commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and present to FP&A and Revenue Ops on Tuesday.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit_term_sheet_v1.pdf

Soojin / team —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from Stratus:

- Pilot start: target Oct 26 (need guaranteed 40 GPUs available on that date).
- Validation criteria for auto-switch: 99th percentile latency < 350ms for chat workload and 85% GPU utilization in steady-state window.
- Billing: we prefer monthly invoicing for the pilot, then net-45 for the long-term commit.

We can accept the auto-switch so long as the acceptance test is clearly defined and our seat at the weekly cadence continues during the pilot. I've copied acct-success for billing alignment.

Regards,
Jennifer Park
VP of Product, StratusAI

All —

Quick follow-up after reading Jennifer's acceptance criteria:

- Ben: we can meet the Oct 26 pilot start if we allocate 40 GPUs from the West US pool and prioritize H100 >=40% for the first two weeks. That requires shifting two burst pools; operational impact is low but we'll need a runbook for fallback.
- Legal/Contracts note: I checked our playbook — auto-switch clauses have been approved at director level if the acceptance criteria are metricized and observed for at least 14 continuous days. Exec signing is only required if the auto-switch includes early termination penalties.

Next steps: Ben to share the runbook draft; Laura to circulate the term sheet to FP&A; Karthik to update the deal stage in HubSpot. I'll schedule a 30-min runway sync for Monday to finalize the runbook and billing cadence.

Marcus Lin
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
